angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 361,764 km at 162.22 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1645 +/- 0.0282 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 162.22 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.52 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Cañas et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5293 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...30C/abstract): 361,764 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.54 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Cañas et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5293 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...30C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3586 +/- 88 K from Cañas et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5293 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...30C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cañas et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5293 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...30C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5293-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.738, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
